newsitem.title: USA: HANOVER RE SETTLES WITH EMLICO JOINT LIQUIDATORS.
newsitem.headline: HANOVER RE SETTLES WITH EMLICO JOINT LIQUIDATORS.

text.p: Electric Mutual Liability Insurance Co has reached a settlement with another of its reinsurers, the joint liquidators of EMLICO said on Wednesday.
German reinsurer Hanover Re agreed to drop all ongoing arbitration and litigation and provide coverage under its reinsurance agreements with EMLICO.
However, the specific terms of the agreement are confidential, the liquidators said.
The settlement with Hanover Re comes less than a month after a similar agreement with General Re Corp.
EMLICO's dispute with its reinsurers stems from its controversial move to Bermuda from Beverly, Mass., in 1995.
Shortly after moving to Bermuda, EMLICO, whose sole policyholder is General Electric Co, declared insolvency.
EMLICO's reinsurers have claimed that regulators were misled into approving the move so that General Electric could take advantage of Bermuda's more favorable insolvency laws.
General Electric has said the reinsurers are simply trying to avoid paying their bills.
EMLICO still has not reached a settlement with Kemper Re and certain syndicates of Lloyd's, a spokesman for the liquidators said.
Kemper Re has appealed a Bermuda court's refusal to grant a judicial review of EMLICO's relocation to the highest court of appeal for British dependent territories.

Meanwhile, a Massachusetts Supreme Court justice has ruled that a dispute between EMLICO and several of its reinsurers was serious enough to warrant consideration by a full court rather than a single judge.
